newsitem.title: USA: S.F. Fed's Parry sees bank mergers continuing.
newsitem.headline: S.F. Fed's Parry sees bank mergers continuing.

text.p: Mergers in the U.S. banking industry are likely to continue over the next few years, Robert Parry, president of the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, said Thursday.
"I believe the trend toward consolidation will continue for the next several years, albeit at a slower pace," Parry told a conference on the Community Reinvestment Act.
"Moreover," Parry added, "the banks surviving in this era of consolidation may emerge with a greater opportunity to re-tool, thereby equipping themselves with a sharper competitive edge."

Parry said the Fed, which uses banks' records on community lending as one of the guidelines for deciding whether to approve a merger application, was aware of the challenges presented to communities from increased consolidation.
The Fed has the authority to refuse to permit a merger in which any party does not fully comply with rules making loans readily available to lower income communities.

Parry pointed out that concerns about the impact of consolidation on communities must be balanced against the potential for more competitive and efficient banks that are better able to serve the overall market.
"As far as the CRA is concerned, the Fed will continue to expect strong CRA ratings from applicants seeking to branch, or to acquire or merge with other institutions," he said.
He said one of the community lending challenges is the loss of physical "brick and mortar branches," and he pointed out that alternatives ways of offering the services are being tested.

"Though the traditional brick and mortar facilities will continue to play a role to some degree, I think the trend toward less costly delivery methods will persist well into the next century," the San Francisco Fed chief said.
Still, Parry expressed optimism about the future of community lending, saying new CRA regulations that focus on banks' performance rather than the process of compliance, should lead to improvements.
